skill.name: testing
skill.description: Guide teams in writing, organizing, and running Deno tests with consistent coverage expectations.
skill.summary: Testing guidance for Deno projects using colocated test files and clear coverage standards.
skill.author: 5t111111

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are Markdown inline code spans, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The skill is prompt-only testing guidance with no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: - Write tests in separate files with the `.test.ts` extension in the same
- Use the command `mise run test` to run all tests in the project

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown inline code for the `.test.ts` filename extension. It does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or user-controlled input.
Line 24 documents a fixed project test command in Markdown. It is normal testing guidance, not executable code in the skill itself.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent test structure and clear coverage expectations. This skill guides Deno test writing, file placement, edge case coverage, and test execution.
actual_capabilities: Recommends the built-in Deno testing framework for tests.
Defines the `.test.ts` file naming convention for test files.
Advises placing tests beside the code they cover.
Requires tests for public functions and methods.
Encourages descriptive test names, edge cases, and error handling.
Specifies `mise run test` as the project test command.
limitations: Does not provide full test templates or assertion examples.
Does not explain mocking, fixtures, or integration test setup.
Assumes the project uses Deno and has a `mise run test` task.
Does not cover CI configuration or coverage reporting.

use_cases.title: Deno Feature Testing
use_cases.description: Plan tests for a new Deno feature with file placement, public API coverage, edge cases, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Check whether a change includes clear tests before it is approved or merged.

use_cases.title: Team Test Standards
use_cases.description: Define simple testing expectations for contributors working in the same Deno codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Deno tests for this module. Use `.test.ts` files beside the source and include descriptive test names.

prompt_templates.title: Review Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my test plan for [feature]. Check whether public functions, edge cases, and error handling are covered.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Test Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a testing checklist for this Deno project. Include file placement, naming, edge cases, error handling, and the `mise run test` step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this pull request for testing gaps. Identify missing public function tests, weak case names, uncovered edge cases, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Add tests for a new date parser.
output_examples.output: Place a date parser test file beside the module. Cover valid dates, invalid formats, timezone boundaries, and parser errors.

output_examples.input: Prepare a pull request for review.
output: Confirm each public function has a matching test.
Check that test names describe expected behavior.
Run the project test command before submission.

output_examples.output: Look for missing edge cases, weak error handling coverage, and unclear test names. Prioritize public APIs first.

best_practices: Create test files beside the source files they cover.
Write clear test names that explain the behavior under review.
Cover public APIs, edge cases, and error handling before committing.
anti_patterns: Leaving public functions without corresponding tests.
Using vague test names that hide the expected behavior.
Submitting changes before running the project test suite.

faq.question: What kind of projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Deno and TypeScript projects that use colocated test files and a project test command.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete test files?
faq.answer: It gives testing guidance and structure. Users must provide project code and exact behavior for complete tests.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only and does not require network access or external services.

faq.question: What test command does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends using the project's `mise run test` command to run all tests.

faq.question: What testing gaps does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes public API coverage, descriptive names, edge cases, and error handling.
